clue.text: Trade Union splits bound to intensify

indicators.note: the union cuts the jump in two, so its letters sit inside the other word

parts.note: a bound is a hop or leap

explanation.surface: A union's internal divisions are certain to make a dispute worse.
explanation.definitionFit: To intensify something is to make it heat up or become fiercer, a common phrasal verb.

clue.text: Old habit damned hard now to break

indicators.note: breaking the words apart and reassembling them signals a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cursed old addiction that is very difficult to give up right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' tempts as an addiction, but here it is clothing, as in a riding habit; 'to break' rearranges DAMNED, H and NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-me-down is a used garment passed on from someone else, and a habit is a garment.

clue.text: Climbing bunk to achieve height

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: bunk means nonsense, rot

explanation.surface: Going up a bunk bed to reach a high spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a rocky hill or peak, especially on Dartmoor, so a height.

clue.text: Page covers test prints

parts.note: roofs are the covers over buildings

explanation.surface: A page wraps around some trial copies from the printer.
explanation.definitionFit: Proofs are trial impressions printed so that a text can be checked before publication.

clue.text: Water having steam as an alternative form

indicators.note: the letters are put into another form, a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Water that can exist in another state, such as vapour.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about water turning to steam; the definition is a particular body of water between Australia and New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tasman Sea is a stretch of ocean, so a body of water.

clue.text: Emerging from that place, present priest with medal after time

indicators.note: after puts the time letter at the front of the other pieces

parts.note: present means here, in attendance
FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Coming out of a place where a priest is presented with a decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The formal adverb means out of or from that thing or place, describing what issues from it.

clue.text: Fed up being put on schedule but left out

indicators.note: out says the letter for left is removed

parts.note: something slated is scheduled or put on a list

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed at being given a timetable that omits them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' reads as annoyed, but it means having eaten one's fill.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fully fed has had enough food, so they are satisfied or full.

clue.text: City article held up for the auditors

indicators.note: auditors are listeners, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: the article A plus delayed, held up

explanation.surface: An item in a newspaper postponed for the accountants checking the books.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the capital of South Australia, a major city.

clue.text: Hang around in order to see well camouflaged creature

parts.note: to stick is to stay or remain somewhere
taken as written
a religious order is a sect

explanation.surface: Loiter somewhere so as to spot something hard to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' is a religious group here, not a sequence or a command.
explanation.definitionFit: Stick insects mimic twigs so closely that they are a classic example of camouflage.

clue.text: Pained expression of agreement about chapter

indicators.note: about says the agreement word goes around the chapter letters

parts.note: aye, also spelt ay, means yes

explanation.surface: A reluctant yes given to a section of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling aches is being in pain, so the adjective matches pained.

clue.text: Dart inside retreat that's most cramped

indicators.note: inside puts the dart within the retreat

parts.note: a nest is a snug retreat or hideaway
an arrow is a dart, a missile

explanation.surface: A dart thrown into the tightest little hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrowest is the superlative of narrow, so the tightest or most confined.

clue.text: Girl's husband after change for publication

indicators.note: after puts the husband letter at the end

parts.note: to edit a text is to revise it before it is published

explanation.surface: A woman whose spouse comes after a revised manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith is a girl's name, the kind of example crosswords call a girl.

clue.text: Staff, keeping discipline, set off for work

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it

indicators.note: keeping means holding the discipline word within the other

parts.note: to spark is to set off or trigger
a field is an area of study, a discipline

explanation.surface: Employees, retaining their sense of order, head out to their jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off' means trigger, not depart, and 'work' is a literary work: Jane Austen's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Mansfield Park is a novel by Jane Austen, so a literary work.

clue.text: There's no virtue in them running old newsreel

indicators.note: running means the letters move about freely into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An outdated film bulletin is screened, though it has no merit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ne'er-do-wells are idle, worthless people with no good qualities.

clue.text: Side notes alarming changes before cracking up

indicators.note: changes signals the word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: A1 or AI means first-class, cracking

explanation.surface: Notes in the margin warning that a breakdown is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes' rearranges the clue's alarming, and 'up' turns the first-rate pair. 'Cracking up' looks like a breakdown, but 'cracking' means excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Marginalia are notes written in the margins of a book, beside the text.

clue.text: Actor's foreword finally completed for poet?

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word

parts.note: o'er is the poetic contraction of over, finished

explanation.surface: An actor's introduction, at last finished, intended for a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of o'er is ignored in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is one who acts, a doer, someone who does things.

clue.text: Proper commotion, with knights confronting a lady centre stage

parts.note: prim means proper and formal
ado is fuss or commotion
N is the chess notation for a knight, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A real stir as knights face a woman in the spotlight.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima donna is the leading female singer in an opera, the star on stage.

clue.text: Traffic warden gives me help after accepting call

indicators.note: accepting means taking the word for call inside

parts.note: taken as written
aid means help
to term something is to call or name it

explanation.surface: A parking official assists the speaker once a phone call is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A meter maid is an informal name for a female traffic warden checking parking meters.

clue.text: Poorly, if externally sound as a bell and improving slightly

indicators.note: externally means the bell sound sits outside the other word

parts.note: a ting is the ringing sound of a bell
poorly means unwell, weak

explanation.surface: Someone unwell though outwardly healthy and on the mend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound as a bell' reads as perfectly healthy, but it is the noise a bell makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweaking is making small adjustments to improve something a little.

clue.text: Significant contribution one had put in impresses small child

indicators.note: put in means placed within the other word

parts.note: to wow is to impress
I'd is the contraction of I had, with I as one
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A big gift a person had made amazes a little one.
explanation.walkthrough: The widow's mite, from the Gospels, is a tiny gift that counted for more because the giver was poor.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical phrase names a small offering that is significant because it is all the giver has.

clue.text: Composer's live recording moving all inside

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: removing all the inner letters leaves just the first and last of the word

explanation.surface: A composer's concert recording with everything within shifted about.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School.

clue.text: President's successor to do without one once more

parts.note: in the sol-fa scale re is the note after do

indicators.note: without means the letter for one is removed

parts.note: again means once more
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The president's replacement has to manage without a single one again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is the first note of the sol-fa scale, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was the 40th President of the United States.

clue.text: Watered plant, worried about area being exposed to elements

indicators.note: about says the other pieces wrap around the area letter

parts.note: wet means watered
a herb is a plant
eaten as in what's eating you means worried

explanation.surface: A watered plant fretting over its patch outdoors in the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts the area letter inside the watered word, right after its first two letters; the definition is weather damage outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather-beaten describes something worn and damaged by long exposure to wind and rain.

clue.text: That gift was removed from cases in Middle East city

indicators.note: taking each word out of its case strips off its outer letters

explanation.surface: A present was taken out of its boxes in a city in the region.
explanation.definitionFit: Haifa is a port city in northern Israel, in the Middle East.

clue.text: A short riddle brings expression of incredulity

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to riddle is to sieve, or sift

explanation.surface: A brief puzzle prompts a disbelieving reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' looks like a puzzle but means a sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: As if is said sarcastically to show disbelief that something could happen.

clue.text: Conductor put back in circuit lost

indicators.note: put back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An electrical conductor restored in a broken circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests electricity, but it is Georg Solti, the orchestral conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Georg Solti was a celebrated Hungarian-British orchestral conductor.

clue.text: Maiden during summer in the country's heading off

parts.note: in means during
AUG, August, is a summer month

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: rural means in the country

explanation.surface: A girl in a rural place during the summer goes away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' looks like a girl, but it is an adjective as in maiden speech or voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden voyage or speech is a first one, which is what an inaugural one is.

clue.text: Rent not quite ready

indicators.note: not quite means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: ripe fruit is ready to eat

explanation.surface: Rent money that is not entirely ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like payment for housing, but it is a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent is a tear or split in fabric, and so is a rip.

clue.text: Port getting heat off fire is hot, mind

indicators.note: off means the word for heat is removed

parts.note: taken as written
ire is anger, heat of passion
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
to mind something is to guard it

explanation.surface: A harbour where a screen keeps warmth from the fire and protects the room.
explanation.walkthrough: FISHGUARD is a ferry port in Pembrokeshire, Wales; the surface suggests a fireguard.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishguard is a Welsh harbour town with a ferry service to Ireland, so a port.

clue.text: Sort of kid, perhaps, who snoozes when listening?

indicators.note: listening means the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: one who naps is a napper

explanation.surface: A child type, maybe someone who dozes, as heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but it is kidskin leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Nappa is a soft leather made from sheepskin or kidskin, so a kind of kid.
